1	# Multi-Cache AMO Coherence — Design
2	
3	**Scope:** the behavior of RISC-V "A"-extension atomics across a multi-cache
4	hierarchy (4× L1 → 1× L2 and 4× L2 → 1× L3), in both the RTL
5	([`hw/rtl/cache/VX_amo_unit.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_amo_unit.sv),
6	[`VX_cache_bank.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_bank.sv),
7	[`VX_cache_tags.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_tags.sv),
8	[`VX_cache_mshr.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_mshr.sv)) and the SimX model
9	([`sim/simx/amo/`](../../sim/simx/amo/),
10	[`sim/simx/mem/cache.cpp`](../../sim/simx/mem/cache.cpp)).
11	
12	This document builds on the single-LLC atomics design
13	([`atomic_memory_operations.md`](atomic_memory_operations.md)) — the decode,
14	LSU sideband, AMO ALU, and "atomics resolve at the last-level cache (LLC)"
15	foundation are described there and assumed here.
16	
17	**Coherence model:** GPU-weak / PULL, matching NVIDIA, ARM Mali, and
18	Imagination PowerVR — atomics resolve at the LLC; inner caches are
19	write-through and not hardware-coherent; cross-core *plain-data* visibility
20	is restored by consumer-side invalidation at acquire points, not by snooping.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 1. The problem
25	
26	Resolving every atomic at the LLC bank is sufficient for a single L1 (the L1
27	*is* the LLC). Once L2 (or L2+L3) is enabled, three things must hold that a
28	naive single-LLC design does not provide:
29	
30	1. **LR/SC forward progress under contention** — every hart must eventually
31	   win its `SC`, independent of how many harts contend.
32	2. **Atomic correctness across levels** — an atomic arriving at a non-LLC
33	   bank must be forwarded to the LLC (which owns the RMW) and its result
34	   routed back, without leaving a stale or duplicate copy behind.
35	3. **Issuer self-consistency** — a hart that issues an atomic and later does
36	   a plain load of the same address must observe its own update, even though
37	   its L1 is write-through and non-coherent.
38	
39	A *fourth* concern — a **plain load on another core** holding a stale copy
40	of an atomically-updated line — is the GPU-weak model's deferred case
41	(Regime B, §6), resolved by a consumer acquire-invalidate exactly as
42	`ld.acquire` / `__threadfence` do on a real GPU.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## 2. Reference architecture: how GPUs do this
47	
48	The cross-vendor pattern is unanimous and is **PULL**, not directory-based:
49	
50	- **Atomics resolve at the shared L2 / memory partition** by dedicated RMW
51	  ALUs, with the target line locked for the duration (the serialization
52	  point). NVIDIA performs the RMW at each memory partition's Atomic
53	  Operation Unit; PowerVR reserves the L2 line so it "cannot be read or
54	  written until the atomic operation has been completely processed"; Mali
55	  resolves atomics near the L2 coherency point.
56	- **Per-core L1 caches are write-through and not hardware-coherent.** Mali:
57	  "coherency is guaranteed only for the LSC; the driver manages the other
58	  caches." NVIDIA: write-through L1 with non-coherent stores that reach the
59	  level "at which a cache coherency policy is enforced" (L2).
60	- **Cross-core visibility is restored at synchronization points** by
61	  flush/invalidate, not snooping — the consumer-side bulk L1 invalidate
62	  behind `ld.acquire` / `__threadfence`.
63	
64	Sources: [GPU atomics @ memory partition (HPCA'13)](https://www2.cs.sfu.ca/~ashriram/papers/2013_HPCA_GPUCoherence.pdf),
65	[non-coherent write-through L1 (US 9047197)](https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9047197),
66	[barrier-initiated flush/invalidate (US 9563561)](https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9563561),
67	[PowerVR L2-locked atomics (US 8108610)](https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/8108610),
68	[Mali Bifrost (Hot Chips 28)](https://old.hotchips.org/wp-content/uploads/hc_archives/hc28/HC28.22-Monday-Epub/HC28.22.10-GPU-HPC-Epub/HC28.22.110-Bifrost-JemDavies-ARM-v04-9.pdf).
69	
70	Vortex already resolves atomics at the LLC and enforces write-through inner
71	caches ([`Vortex.sv`](../../hw/rtl/Vortex.sv),
72	[`processor.cpp`](../../sim/simx/processor.cpp)); this design adds the
73	forwarding, self-consistency, and consumer-invalidate pieces.
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 3. Design decisions
78	
79	| Question | Decision | Rationale |
80	|---|---|---|
81	| Coherence scope | AMO-triggered, weak (GPU) model | Plain store→load across cores stays the programmer's responsibility (fences), as on every real GPU. Smallest change. |
82	| How is a remote stale copy cleaned? | **PULL** | The consumer invalidates its *own* inner cache at an acquire fence; the LLC never pushes invalidations upward (what NVIDIA/Mali do; least code). |
83	| Topology | Same cache module at every level | The mechanism lives inside the one reusable cache; recursion to L3 is free (§5.6). |
84	| Reservation tracking | **Per hart** | One reservation per hart matches RISC-V and guarantees forward progress (§5.1). |
85	
86	**Rejected: PUSH + directory/snoop-filter.** Back-invalidating remote inner
87	caches from the LLC would make atomics coherent with no software fence, but
88	needs an upstream back-probe channel, a per-line sharer directory, an
89	ack/ordering protocol, and recursive re-probing — a whole coherence
90	subsystem that does not scale O(cores) and that real GPUs avoid. Recorded as
91	future work (§7).
92	
93	---
94	
95	## 4. Core invariant and the two regimes
96	
97	> **An atomic never leaves a copy of its line in any inner (non-LLC) cache.**
98	
99	It holds because (a) the requesting cache self-invalidates the line as the
100	atomic is forwarded down, (b) the atomic is non-allocating, so no fill is
101	installed afterward, and (c) the atomic never touches sibling inner caches.
102	The only way an inner cache can hold a line being atomically updated is a
103	**plain load** on that core. This splits all behavior into two regimes:
104	
105	- **Regime A — atomic-only sharing** (spinlock, atomic counter; the common
106	  case). No inner cache ever holds the line; every atomic serializes at the
107	  LLC. **Fully implemented and validated.** Zero new coherence traffic.
108	- **Regime B — a plain load cached the line on another core.** That copy is
109	  stale after a remote atomic. Resolved by the consumer's acquire-invalidate
110	  (§7), exactly as a GPU requires `ld.acquire` / `__threadfence`. **Deferred**
111	  until a mixed atomic/plain-load workload needs it.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. Mechanisms (implemented)
116	
117	Each mechanism is realized in both SimX and RTL. The SimX model was brought
118	up first as the goal-reference oracle; the RTL mirrors its behavior at the
119	cache-bank microarchitecture.
120	
121	### 5.1 Per-hart LR/SC reservations
122	
123	A shared, capacity-bounded reservation table with LRU eviction does not
124	guarantee forward progress: once contending harts exceed the table size, a
125	hart's reservation can be evicted by another hart's `LR` between its own `LR`
126	and `SC`, so the `SC` never succeeds (`lrsc_counter` hangs at ≥ 64 harts).
127	
128	The reservation store is **per hart** — each hart owns exactly one
129	reservation, never displaced by another hart's `LR`, broken only by a
130	committed write to the line. This matches RISC-V (a reservation is a property
131	of the hart) and guarantees a winner each retry round.
132	
133	- **SimX:** a `hart_id → line` map in
134	  [`amo_unit.{h,cpp}`](../../sim/simx/amo/amo_unit.cpp).
135	- **RTL:** a directly-indexed array of `NUM_HARTS = 1 << HART_ID_WIDTH` slots
136	  `{valid, line_addr}` in [`VX_amo_unit.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_amo_unit.sv);
137	  `reserve`/`check` index the requester's slot, `invalidate` clears matching
138	  slots of other harts. `VX_CFG_AMO_RS_SIZE` is retained for compatibility
139	  and no longer bounds correctness.
140	
141	### 5.2 Plain-write reservation invalidation
142	
143	The LLC breaks a hart's reservation on **any** committed write to the
144	reserved line, not only atomic stores, so a plain store from another hart
145	fails a racing `SC`. SimX pulses `invalidate(line, except=hart)` on every LLC
146	write-through path; RTL drives `amo_res_invalidate_w = amo_do_store_st1 ||
147	do_write_st1` into the AMO unit.
148	
149	### 5.3 Non-LLC AMO passthrough
150	
151	A non-LLC bank does not own the atomic. It forwards the AMO downstream
152	non-allocating and routes the result word back up.
153	
154	- **SimX:** an `AmoProbe` ([`cache.cpp`](../../sim/simx/mem/cache.cpp))
155	  probes the local line, invalidates on hit, and forwards without installing
156	  a fill.
157	- **RTL:** the existing miss→fill→replay path is **reused** rather than
158	  adding a separate side-table ([`VX_cache_bank.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_bank.sv)
159	  `g_amo_ptw`). The AMO allocates a normal MSHR entry, flagged in a parallel
160	  `amo_ptw_flag[]` with the result word-select in `amo_ptw_wsel[]`. On the
161	  downstream fill the flagged entry captures the result word, **installs no
162	  line**, and replays carrying the result up to `core_rsp`
163	  (`eff_hit_st1 = is_hit_st1 || is_amo_replay_st1`). AMOs are excluded from
164	  MSHR coalescing (`amo_table` masks them out of `addr_matches`, and the
165	  requester is forced non-pending) so each atomic takes its own round-trip;
166	  at the LLC, same-line AMO coalescing is preserved (`allocate_is_amo` gated
167	  to non-LLC).
168	
169	### 5.4 Issuer self-consistency
170	
171	A hart that issues an atomic and later plain-loads the same address must see
172	its own update. As the atomic is forwarded, the issuing cache invalidates its
173	local copy so the next load misses and refetches from the LLC. In SimX this
174	falls out of the `AmoProbe` self-invalidate; in RTL,
175	[`VX_cache_tags.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_tags.sv) gains an
176	`invalidate` input that clears `line_valid` on a tag match (using a raw hit
177	that excludes a line being filled this cycle), driven by
178	`is_amo_fwd_st0 && is_hit_st0`.
179	
180	### 5.5 AMO/fill age-ordering
181	
182	A load-then-AMO (or AMO-then-load) to the same line can race the
183	probe/invalidate against an in-flight fill in the bank pipeline. Symmetric
184	age-ordering holds the younger access at admission until the older drains:
185	
186	- an incoming AMO waits while a load fill is pending for its line (so its
187	  invalidate lands on the installed line);
188	- an incoming plain load waits while an AMO passthrough is pending for its
189	  line (so the load observes the AMO — same-hart same-address program order).
190	
191	SimX defers the `AmoProbe` in `processInputs` and re-issues a vanished-line
192	replay as a fresh miss. RTL uses MSHR probe ports
193	(`probe_pending_ld` / `probe_pending_amo`,
194	[`VX_cache_mshr.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_mshr.sv)) to drive
195	`amo_input_defer` / `load_input_defer` at the bank input, plus a same-cycle
196	allocation guard for the admit→allocate window.
197	
198	### 5.6 LLC AMO commit-window serialization (RTL)
199	
200	The LLC AMO writeback path is single-outstanding (it chains only same-line
201	AMOs). Admitting a second AMO to a different line while the first is still in
202	its writeback window would let it reach S1 with the writeback busy and drop
203	its store. The bank closes the whole window — `amo_commit_busy = amo_wb_pending
204	|| amo_do_store_st1 || amo_do_store_st0` gates the AMO request path and
205	`core_req_ready`. All terms are zero at non-LLC banks, so this serialization
206	applies only at the LLC.
207	
208	### 5.7 Recursion to L3 is free
209	
210	The mechanism is per-cache and the same cache module is instantiated at every
211	level. An atomic under an L3 config travels L1→L2→L3, self-invalidating L1
212	**and** L2 on the way down (both act as non-LLC), and the L3 performs the RMW.
213	No per-level special-casing and no inter-level messaging beyond the normal
214	request flow. The `AMO_ENABLE` parameter on each cache is driven by
215	`VX_CFG_EXT_A_ENABLED` alone (not gated to the LLC), so non-LLC data caches
216	synthesize the passthrough; the LLC-vs-passthrough distinction is made inside
217	the bank.
218	
219	---
220	
221	## 6. Worked walkthroughs
222	
223	### 6.1 4× L1 → 1× L2 (L2 = LLC)
224	
225	```
226	   core0   core1   core2   core3
227	    L1_0    L1_1    L1_2    L1_3      write-through, non-coherent
228	      └──────┴───┬───┴──────┘
229	                 L2 (LLC: RMW + per-hart reservations)
230	                 memory
231	```
232	
233	**Regime A — `amoadd counter` by all cores:** each core's atomic invalidates
234	its own L1 copy of `counter` and increments at L2; no L1 ever holds
235	`counter`; the final value and the unique fetch-add returns are correct with
236	zero cross-L1 traffic.
237	
238	**Regime B — producer/consumer via a plain load:** if `core0` previously
239	plain-loaded `flag` (caching it) and `core3` then `amoadd flag,1`, `core0`'s
240	next plain load hits its stale L1 copy until `core0` issues an
241	acquire-invalidate (§7), after which it misses and refetches the current
242	value from L2. The L2 never reaches up.
243	
244	### 6.2 4× L2 → 1× L3 (L3 = LLC)
245	
246	```
247	 cluster0           ...            cluster3
248	 L1×4 → L2_0                       L1×4 → L2_3
249	    └───────────────┬─────────────────┘
250	                  L3 (LLC: RMW + per-hart reservations)
251	                  memory
252	```
253	
254	A core in cluster0 doing `amoadd X` self-invalidates **L1 and L2_0** en route
255	(both non-LLC) and the L3 performs the RMW. Identical mechanism, one extra
256	level traversed, no new code.
257	
258	---
259	
260	## 7. Deferred: Regime-B acquire-invalidate
261	
262	The one unimplemented piece is the consumer-side **bulk invalidate** at an
263	acquire synchronization point — clearing the inner cache's valid bits (no
264	writeback; inner caches are write-through, never dirty) so the next plain load
265	refetches from the LLC. The design reuses the existing flush walk with an
266	invalidate mode and routes a `FENCE`/acquire through the LSU as a new memory
267	op on the existing core→cache path — no new fabric channel. It is deferred
268	until a mixed atomic/plain-load workload requires fence-managed cross-core
269	data visibility.
270	
271	---
272	
273	## 8. Elastic cache-bank pipeline (configurable latency)
274	
275	[`VX_cache_bank.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_bank.sv) supports a
276	per-cache pipeline depth `LATENCY` (from `VX_CFG_<CACHE>_LATENCY`, default
277	`2` = the classic lookup/commit pipe, reproduced bit-for-bit). A small,
278	latency-critical L1 wants depth 2; a large last-level cache cannot close
279	300 MHz at depth 2 because the tag read, the way-resolving compare, and the
280	data-array access are crammed into one cycle, producing a BRAM→BRAM critical
281	path whose delay is ~78 % routing and cannot be retimed away. Raising the
282	knob inserts register stages on the long paths, trading a few cycles of hit
283	latency — which the non-blocking, MSHR-backed cache hides — for Fmax. This is
284	how real GPU L2/L3 caches are built: deep, fully pipelined, latency-tolerant
285	behind a large miss pool.
286	
287	### 8.1 Motivating timing data
288	
289	Post-route WNS on the standalone `Vortex` DUT (`xcu55c`, 300 MHz, after the
290	dirty-mask LUTRAM fix), 2-core build with the 1 MB 8-way L2:
291	
292	| Config | WNS @300 MHz | Implied Fmax | Worst path |
293	|--------|-------------:|-------------:|------------|
294	| L2 write-back    | **−1.380 ns** | ~212 MHz | `tag_store` → `data_store` EN/WE |
295	| L2 write-through | **−1.008 ns** | ~230 MHz | same structure |
296	
297	The path sits in the L2, so the *whole device* is capped at ~210–230 MHz; the
298	single-cycle BRAM→BRAM dependency cannot be placed/routed away — the cycle
299	boundary must move.
300	
301	### 8.2 Bank pipeline structure
302	
303	The bank carries all per-request control/data in a packed payload struct
304	through a generate-loop register chain of depth `LATENCY` (replacing the
305	hand-instantiated `_sel`/`_st0`/`_st1` wires), with control anchored to
306	**symbolic stage indices** so the feedback loops stay one-request-per-cycle
307	at any depth:
308	
309	```
310	HIT_ST  = TAG_RD_LAT        // tag compare consumes stg[HIT_ST]
311	DATA_ST = HIT_ST + 1        // data access uses *registered* way
312	RESP_ST = LATENCY - 1       // crsp / mem-req fire here
313	```
314	
315	The whole data-array access (read **and** write, plus fill/flush) is deferred
316	together by `PIPE_EX = LATENCY-2` stages so the data BRAM is driven by
317	*registered* `tag_matches`/way/line/byteen — the tag-compare→data-EN and
318	→data-addr paths (bottlenecks 1 and 2 above) become register→BRAM,
319	intra-stage. Because read and write move to the *same* deferred stage,
320	pipeline order is preserved (a younger same-line read always reaches the
321	array after an older write), so store→load forwarding is automatic — **no
322	1R1W split, no forwarding logic, no hazard scoreboard** beyond the same-line
323	AMO pacing (§8.4). The tag array stays at S0/S1, so its existing
324	read-during-write bypasses (`rdw_fill`/`rdw_write`) are unchanged.
325	
326	### 8.3 The MSHR must NOT be deferred (critical constraint)
327	
328	[`VX_cache_mshr.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_mshr.sv) is strongly coupled
329	to the bank: its coalescing chain needs `allocate` (S0) and `finalize` (S1)
330	**exactly one cycle apart**. The tail-find (`prev_idx`) only sees a
331	predecessor's link once that predecessor finalizes; deferring finalize makes
332	3+ coalesced same-line misses (e.g. sequential icache fetches to one line)
333	all link to the same predecessor, orphaning intermediate entries → they never
334	replay → **bank deadlock** (confirmed empirically — a naive "defer
335	everything" hung at LATENCY=3 and 4). So the pipeline is **decoupled**:
336	
337	- **S0/S1 (fixed, 1 cycle apart):** tag compare, replacement victim-select,
338	  MSHR allocate **and** finalize, replacement update — untouched.
339	- **stD = S0 + PIPE_EX:** data-array access (pass-through chain off S0).
340	- **stC = S1 + PIPE_EX:** core response + memory request (off S1), aligned
341	  with the deferred data output.
342	
343	`PIPE_EX=0` collapses stD→S0, stC→S1, reproducing the 2-stage bank exactly
344	(LATENCY=2 gives identical cycle counts).
345	
346	**Mem-request queue sizing:** the mem-req push now fires `LATENCY` stages
347	after admission, so the almost-full margin must reserve `LATENCY` slots —
348	**`MREQ_SIZE > LATENCY`** (else `ALM_FULL ≤ 0` → permanent almost-full →
349	admission deadlock). The config grows `MREQ_SIZE` by `(LATENCY−2)` to hold
350	the margin constant.
351	
352	### 8.4 AMO under elastic latency
353	
354	The LLC atomic (§5.6) is the most stage-coupled block. Under the elastic pipe
355	its anchors are re-expressed on the symbolic stage constants rather than
356	literal `st0`/`st1`: the RMW reads the line word at the data-output stage,
357	runs the AMO ALU (add/min/max/swap/compare) in the following stage, and
358	writes back at the commit stage — so deepening *relaxes* the AMO ALU path
359	(it gets its own stage) rather than complicating it. Same-line AMO chaining
360	(a chained atomic must observe the previous result) has a commit→visible
361	round trip of `L−1` cycles, so the `chain_stall`/`commit_busy` pacing scales
362	with `LATENCY` and **collapses into one depth-sized same-line scoreboard**
363	(a chained atomic targets a line that scoreboard already marks in-flight).
364	Non-LLC AMO forward/passthru-replay ordering and LR/SC reservations are
365	event-ordered (line addresses, not cycles), so they are latency-agnostic
366	once keyed off the stage constants. At `LATENCY=2` behavior is identical to
367	today (chain window = 1).
368	
369	### 8.5 Configuration, cost, and SimX parity
370	
371	Per-cache knobs in `VX_config.toml` (default 2; raise large LLCs):
372	
373	```
374	VX_CFG_L2_LATENCY  = expr: 4 if $VX_CFG_L2_CACHE_SIZE > 65536 else 2
375	VX_CFG_L3_LATENCY  = expr: 4 if $VX_CFG_L3_CACHE_SIZE > 65536 else 2
376	VX_CFG_L2_MREQ_SIZE = expr: 4 + ($VX_CFG_L2_LATENCY - 2) + ...   # keep margin
377	```
378	
379	The 64 KB threshold: below it the tag/data arrays fit in a few adjacent BRAMs
380	and the single-cycle path closes; above it (1 MB L2, 2 MB L3) the arrays span
381	many BRAM columns and the cross-array route cannot meet 3.333 ns.
382	
383	- **Area** (1 MB L2 bank, depth 2→4): ~+1 % FF (two ~590 b payload stages),
384	  ~0 BRAM (read/write split is BRAM-native dual-port), a few hundred LUT —
385	  cheap for a +42 % clock.
386	- **AMAT:** `Δt_L2 = +2 cyc ⇒ ΔAMAT ≈ m_L1·2 cyc` (~+0.2–0.4 cyc for
387	  `m_L1≈0.1–0.2`), in the noise against a hundreds-of-cycle `t_mem`. The
388	  decisive comparison is wall-clock: a single L2 hit is ~3.9 ns slower but
389	  every cycle everywhere is 42 % faster and the latency is MSHR-hidden.
390	- **SimX parity:** the SimX bank already models a `latency`-deep pipe
391	  (`Cache::Config::latency`); the gap is only that L2/L3 use a hardcoded `2`
392	  ([`cluster.cpp`](../../sim/simx/cluster.cpp),
393	  [`processor.cpp`](../../sim/simx/processor.cpp)) instead of the macro.
394	  Sourcing both the RTL bank parameter and the SimX pipe depth from the same
395	  `VX_CFG_*_LATENCY` keeps them from diverging. The same-line RAW/AMO-chain
396	  stall must also be modeled in the SimX bank (a marked-line check on
397	  `pipe_req_` occupancy) so throughput — not just latency — matches.
398	
399	> Status: `LATENCY=2` is bit-identical to the pre-refactor baseline and
400	> `LATENCY=3` is functionally validated (rtlsim vecadd/sgemm). `LATENCY=4`
401	> (with bumped `MREQ_SIZE`), the AMO sweep across depths, SimX parity wiring,
402	> and the 1 MB-L2 DUT synth confirming WNS ≥ 0 @300 MHz remain to land.
403	> Depends on the `VX_sp_ram`/`VX_dp_ram` `USE_FAST_BRAM` LUTRAM fix.
404	
405	---
406	
407	## 9. Validation
408	
409	`tests/regression/amo` across all configs, on both SimX and rtlsim:
410	
411	| config | result |
412	|---|---|
413	| 1 core, no L2 | 13/13 |
414	| 4× L1 → 1× L2 | 12/12 |
415	| 4× L2 → 1× L3 | 12/12 |
416	
417	The suite includes `lrsc_counter` (forward-progress repro for §5.1) and
418	`self_consistency` (per-hart private 64 B line; exercises §5.4/§5.6 and fails
419	a design lacking the local-invalidate and commit-window serialization).
420	`atomic_critical` is skipped on multi-core: it relies on plain load/store
421	inside a critical section, which needs Regime-B coherence (§7).
422	`rv32ua`/`rv64ua` ISA conformance (LR/SC + all AMOs) passes. The full
423	`regression --cache` suite (L1/L2/L3 enable+disable, banking, ways,
424	replacement policy, writeback, clustering, reduced line-size) passes,
425	confirming the `AMO_ENABLE` plumbing and bank/tag/MSHR changes do not regress
426	non-AMO cache behavior.
427	
428	Outstanding: xrt sign-off at the multi-core configs and U55C @ 300 MHz timing
429	closure. The new state is the per-hart reservation array (scales with
430	`NUM_HARTS`) and the per-MSHR-entry passthrough word table; if the §5.1
431	`invalidate` compare or the §5.4 local-invalidate is critical, it can be
432	pipelined off the SC-success / hit path (both tolerate an extra cycle).
433	
434	---
435	
436	## 10. Out of scope / future work
437	
438	- **Regime-B acquire-invalidate** (§7) — the consumer-side bulk invalidate
439	  for fence-managed cross-core plain-data visibility.
440	- **PUSH + directory/snoop-filter** — fence-free cross-core plain-data
441	  coherence; requires an upstream back-probe channel, per-line sharer
442	  tracking, an ack/ordering protocol, and recursive re-probing. Not what GPUs
443	  do; revisit only if a strong cross-core guarantee is ever required.
444	- **Per-line acquire invalidate** — finer-grained than the whole-cache flash
445	  invalidate, if profiling shows bulk invalidation hurts hit rate.
446	- The RTL AMO unit testbench and AMO performance counters
447	  ([`atomic_memory_operations.md`](atomic_memory_operations.md) §6.3–§6.4).
448

# Multi-Cache AMO Coherence — Design

**Scope:** the behavior of RISC-V "A"-extension atomics across a multi-cache
hierarchy (4× L1 → 1× L2 and 4× L2 → 1× L3), in both the RTL
([`hw/rtl/cache/VX_amo_unit.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_amo_unit.sv),
[`VX_cache_bank.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_bank.sv),
[`VX_cache_tags.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_tags.sv),
[`VX_cache_mshr.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_mshr.sv)) and the SimX model
([`sim/simx/amo/`](../../sim/simx/amo/),
[`sim/simx/mem/cache.cpp`](../../sim/simx/mem/cache.cpp)).

This document builds on the single-LLC atomics design
([`atomic_memory_operations.md`](atomic_memory_operations.md)) — the decode,
LSU sideband, AMO ALU, and "atomics resolve at the last-level cache (LLC)"
foundation are described there and assumed here.

**Coherence model:** GPU-weak / PULL, matching NVIDIA, ARM Mali, and
Imagination PowerVR — atomics resolve at the LLC; inner caches are
write-through and not hardware-coherent; cross-core *plain-data* visibility
is restored by consumer-side invalidation at acquire points, not by snooping.

---

## 1. The problem

Resolving every atomic at the LLC bank is sufficient for a single L1 (the L1
*is* the LLC). Once L2 (or L2+L3) is enabled, three things must hold that a
naive single-LLC design does not provide:

1. **LR/SC forward progress under contention** — every hart must eventually
   win its `SC`, independent of how many harts contend.
2. **Atomic correctness across levels** — an atomic arriving at a non-LLC
   bank must be forwarded to the LLC (which owns the RMW) and its result
   routed back, without leaving a stale or duplicate copy behind.
3. **Issuer self-consistency** — a hart that issues an atomic and later does
   a plain load of the same address must observe its own update, even though
   its L1 is write-through and non-coherent.

A *fourth* concern — a **plain load on another core** holding a stale copy
of an atomically-updated line — is the GPU-weak model's deferred case
(Regime B, §6), resolved by a consumer acquire-invalidate exactly as
`ld.acquire` / `__threadfence` do on a real GPU.

---

## 2. Reference architecture: how GPUs do this

The cross-vendor pattern is unanimous and is **PULL**, not directory-based:

- **Atomics resolve at the shared L2 / memory partition** by dedicated RMW
  ALUs, with the target line locked for the duration (the serialization
  point). NVIDIA performs the RMW at each memory partition's Atomic
  Operation Unit; PowerVR reserves the L2 line so it "cannot be read or
  written until the atomic operation has been completely processed"; Mali
  resolves atomics near the L2 coherency point.
- **Per-core L1 caches are write-through and not hardware-coherent.** Mali:
  "coherency is guaranteed only for the LSC; the driver manages the other
  caches." NVIDIA: write-through L1 with non-coherent stores that reach the
  level "at which a cache coherency policy is enforced" (L2).
- **Cross-core visibility is restored at synchronization points** by
  flush/invalidate, not snooping — the consumer-side bulk L1 invalidate
  behind `ld.acquire` / `__threadfence`.

Sources: [GPU atomics @ memory partition (HPCA'13)](https://www2.cs.sfu.ca/~ashriram/papers/2013_HPCA_GPUCoherence.pdf),
[non-coherent write-through L1 (US 9047197)](https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9047197),
[barrier-initiated flush/invalidate (US 9563561)](https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9563561),
[PowerVR L2-locked atomics (US 8108610)](https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/8108610),
[Mali Bifrost (Hot Chips 28)](https://old.hotchips.org/wp-content/uploads/hc_archives/hc28/HC28.22-Monday-Epub/HC28.22.10-GPU-HPC-Epub/HC28.22.110-Bifrost-JemDavies-ARM-v04-9.pdf).

Vortex already resolves atomics at the LLC and enforces write-through inner
caches ([`Vortex.sv`](../../hw/rtl/Vortex.sv),
[`processor.cpp`](../../sim/simx/processor.cpp)); this design adds the
forwarding, self-consistency, and consumer-invalidate pieces.

---

## 3. Design decisions

| Question | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Coherence scope | AMO-triggered, weak (GPU) model | Plain store→load across cores stays the programmer's responsibility (fences), as on every real GPU. Smallest change. |
| How is a remote stale copy cleaned? | **PULL** | The consumer invalidates its *own* inner cache at an acquire fence; the LLC never pushes invalidations upward (what NVIDIA/Mali do; least code). |
| Topology | Same cache module at every level | The mechanism lives inside the one reusable cache; recursion to L3 is free (§5.6). |
| Reservation tracking | **Per hart** | One reservation per hart matches RISC-V and guarantees forward progress (§5.1). |

**Rejected: PUSH + directory/snoop-filter.** Back-invalidating remote inner
caches from the LLC would make atomics coherent with no software fence, but
needs an upstream back-probe channel, a per-line sharer directory, an
ack/ordering protocol, and recursive re-probing — a whole coherence
subsystem that does not scale O(cores) and that real GPUs avoid. Recorded as
future work (§7).

---

## 4. Core invariant and the two regimes

> **An atomic never leaves a copy of its line in any inner (non-LLC) cache.**

It holds because (a) the requesting cache self-invalidates the line as the
atomic is forwarded down, (b) the atomic is non-allocating, so no fill is
installed afterward, and (c) the atomic never touches sibling inner caches.
The only way an inner cache can hold a line being atomically updated is a
**plain load** on that core. This splits all behavior into two regimes:

- **Regime A — atomic-only sharing** (spinlock, atomic counter; the common
  case). No inner cache ever holds the line; every atomic serializes at the
  LLC. **Fully implemented and validated.** Zero new coherence traffic.
- **Regime B — a plain load cached the line on another core.** That copy is
  stale after a remote atomic. Resolved by the consumer's acquire-invalidate
  (§7), exactly as a GPU requires `ld.acquire` / `__threadfence`. **Deferred**
  until a mixed atomic/plain-load workload needs it.

---

## 5. Mechanisms (implemented)

Each mechanism is realized in both SimX and RTL. The SimX model was brought
up first as the goal-reference oracle; the RTL mirrors its behavior at the
cache-bank microarchitecture.

### 5.1 Per-hart LR/SC reservations

A shared, capacity-bounded reservation table with LRU eviction does not
guarantee forward progress: once contending harts exceed the table size, a
hart's reservation can be evicted by another hart's `LR` between its own `LR`
and `SC`, so the `SC` never succeeds (`lrsc_counter` hangs at ≥ 64 harts).

The reservation store is **per hart** — each hart owns exactly one
reservation, never displaced by another hart's `LR`, broken only by a
committed write to the line. This matches RISC-V (a reservation is a property
of the hart) and guarantees a winner each retry round.

- **SimX:** a `hart_id → line` map in
  [`amo_unit.{h,cpp}`](../../sim/simx/amo/amo_unit.cpp).
- **RTL:** a directly-indexed array of `NUM_HARTS = 1 << HART_ID_WIDTH` slots
  `{valid, line_addr}` in [`VX_amo_unit.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_amo_unit.sv);
  `reserve`/`check` index the requester's slot, `invalidate` clears matching
  slots of other harts. `VX_CFG_AMO_RS_SIZE` is retained for compatibility
  and no longer bounds correctness.

### 5.2 Plain-write reservation invalidation

The LLC breaks a hart's reservation on **any** committed write to the
reserved line, not only atomic stores, so a plain store from another hart
fails a racing `SC`. SimX pulses `invalidate(line, except=hart)` on every LLC
write-through path; RTL drives `amo_res_invalidate_w = amo_do_store_st1 ||
do_write_st1` into the AMO unit.

### 5.3 Non-LLC AMO passthrough

A non-LLC bank does not own the atomic. It forwards the AMO downstream
non-allocating and routes the result word back up.

- **SimX:** an `AmoProbe` ([`cache.cpp`](../../sim/simx/mem/cache.cpp))
  probes the local line, invalidates on hit, and forwards without installing
  a fill.
- **RTL:** the existing miss→fill→replay path is **reused** rather than
  adding a separate side-table ([`VX_cache_bank.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_bank.sv)
  `g_amo_ptw`). The AMO allocates a normal MSHR entry, flagged in a parallel
  `amo_ptw_flag[]` with the result word-select in `amo_ptw_wsel[]`. On the
  downstream fill the flagged entry captures the result word, **installs no
  line**, and replays carrying the result up to `core_rsp`
  (`eff_hit_st1 = is_hit_st1 || is_amo_replay_st1`). AMOs are excluded from
  MSHR coalescing (`amo_table` masks them out of `addr_matches`, and the
  requester is forced non-pending) so each atomic takes its own round-trip;
  at the LLC, same-line AMO coalescing is preserved (`allocate_is_amo` gated
  to non-LLC).

### 5.4 Issuer self-consistency

A hart that issues an atomic and later plain-loads the same address must see
its own update. As the atomic is forwarded, the issuing cache invalidates its
local copy so the next load misses and refetches from the LLC. In SimX this
falls out of the `AmoProbe` self-invalidate; in RTL,
[`VX_cache_tags.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_tags.sv) gains an
`invalidate` input that clears `line_valid` on a tag match (using a raw hit
that excludes a line being filled this cycle), driven by
`is_amo_fwd_st0 && is_hit_st0`.

### 5.5 AMO/fill age-ordering

A load-then-AMO (or AMO-then-load) to the same line can race the
probe/invalidate against an in-flight fill in the bank pipeline. Symmetric
age-ordering holds the younger access at admission until the older drains:

- an incoming AMO waits while a load fill is pending for its line (so its
  invalidate lands on the installed line);
- an incoming plain load waits while an AMO passthrough is pending for its
  line (so the load observes the AMO — same-hart same-address program order).

SimX defers the `AmoProbe` in `processInputs` and re-issues a vanished-line
replay as a fresh miss. RTL uses MSHR probe ports
(`probe_pending_ld` / `probe_pending_amo`,
[`VX_cache_mshr.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_mshr.sv)) to drive
`amo_input_defer` / `load_input_defer` at the bank input, plus a same-cycle
allocation guard for the admit→allocate window.

### 5.6 LLC AMO commit-window serialization (RTL)

The LLC AMO writeback path is single-outstanding (it chains only same-line
AMOs). Admitting a second AMO to a different line while the first is still in
its writeback window would let it reach S1 with the writeback busy and drop
its store. The bank closes the whole window — `amo_commit_busy = amo_wb_pending
|| amo_do_store_st1 || amo_do_store_st0` gates the AMO request path and
`core_req_ready`. All terms are zero at non-LLC banks, so this serialization
applies only at the LLC.

### 5.7 Recursion to L3 is free

The mechanism is per-cache and the same cache module is instantiated at every
level. An atomic under an L3 config travels L1→L2→L3, self-invalidating L1
**and** L2 on the way down (both act as non-LLC), and the L3 performs the RMW.
No per-level special-casing and no inter-level messaging beyond the normal
request flow. The `AMO_ENABLE` parameter on each cache is driven by
`VX_CFG_EXT_A_ENABLED` alone (not gated to the LLC), so non-LLC data caches
synthesize the passthrough; the LLC-vs-passthrough distinction is made inside
the bank.

---

## 6. Worked walkthroughs

### 6.1 4× L1 → 1× L2 (L2 = LLC)

```
   core0   core1   core2   core3
    L1_0    L1_1    L1_2    L1_3      write-through, non-coherent
      └──────┴───┬───┴──────┘
                 L2 (LLC: RMW + per-hart reservations)
                 memory
```

**Regime A — `amoadd counter` by all cores:** each core's atomic invalidates
its own L1 copy of `counter` and increments at L2; no L1 ever holds
`counter`; the final value and the unique fetch-add returns are correct with
zero cross-L1 traffic.

**Regime B — producer/consumer via a plain load:** if `core0` previously
plain-loaded `flag` (caching it) and `core3` then `amoadd flag,1`, `core0`'s
next plain load hits its stale L1 copy until `core0` issues an
acquire-invalidate (§7), after which it misses and refetches the current
value from L2. The L2 never reaches up.

### 6.2 4× L2 → 1× L3 (L3 = LLC)

```
 cluster0           ...            cluster3
 L1×4 → L2_0                       L1×4 → L2_3
    └───────────────┬─────────────────┘
                  L3 (LLC: RMW + per-hart reservations)
                  memory
```

A core in cluster0 doing `amoadd X` self-invalidates **L1 and L2_0** en route
(both non-LLC) and the L3 performs the RMW. Identical mechanism, one extra
level traversed, no new code.

---

## 7. Deferred: Regime-B acquire-invalidate

The one unimplemented piece is the consumer-side **bulk invalidate** at an
acquire synchronization point — clearing the inner cache's valid bits (no
writeback; inner caches are write-through, never dirty) so the next plain load
refetches from the LLC. The design reuses the existing flush walk with an
invalidate mode and routes a `FENCE`/acquire through the LSU as a new memory
op on the existing core→cache path — no new fabric channel. It is deferred
until a mixed atomic/plain-load workload requires fence-managed cross-core
data visibility.

---

## 8. Elastic cache-bank pipeline (configurable latency)

[`VX_cache_bank.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_bank.sv) supports a
per-cache pipeline depth `LATENCY` (from `VX_CFG_<CACHE>_LATENCY`, default
`2` = the classic lookup/commit pipe, reproduced bit-for-bit). A small,
latency-critical L1 wants depth 2; a large last-level cache cannot close
300 MHz at depth 2 because the tag read, the way-resolving compare, and the
data-array access are crammed into one cycle, producing a BRAM→BRAM critical
path whose delay is ~78 % routing and cannot be retimed away. Raising the
knob inserts register stages on the long paths, trading a few cycles of hit
latency — which the non-blocking, MSHR-backed cache hides — for Fmax. This is
how real GPU L2/L3 caches are built: deep, fully pipelined, latency-tolerant
behind a large miss pool.

### 8.1 Motivating timing data

Post-route WNS on the standalone `Vortex` DUT (`xcu55c`, 300 MHz, after the
dirty-mask LUTRAM fix), 2-core build with the 1 MB 8-way L2:

| Config | WNS @300 MHz | Implied Fmax | Worst path |
|--------|-------------:|-------------:|------------|
| L2 write-back    | **−1.380 ns** | ~212 MHz | `tag_store` → `data_store` EN/WE |
| L2 write-through | **−1.008 ns** | ~230 MHz | same structure |

The path sits in the L2, so the *whole device* is capped at ~210–230 MHz; the
single-cycle BRAM→BRAM dependency cannot be placed/routed away — the cycle
boundary must move.

### 8.2 Bank pipeline structure

The bank carries all per-request control/data in a packed payload struct
through a generate-loop register chain of depth `LATENCY` (replacing the
hand-instantiated `_sel`/`_st0`/`_st1` wires), with control anchored to
**symbolic stage indices** so the feedback loops stay one-request-per-cycle
at any depth:

```
HIT_ST  = TAG_RD_LAT        // tag compare consumes stg[HIT_ST]
DATA_ST = HIT_ST + 1        // data access uses *registered* way
RESP_ST = LATENCY - 1       // crsp / mem-req fire here
```

The whole data-array access (read **and** write, plus fill/flush) is deferred
together by `PIPE_EX = LATENCY-2` stages so the data BRAM is driven by
*registered* `tag_matches`/way/line/byteen — the tag-compare→data-EN and
→data-addr paths (bottlenecks 1 and 2 above) become register→BRAM,
intra-stage. Because read and write move to the *same* deferred stage,
pipeline order is preserved (a younger same-line read always reaches the
array after an older write), so store→load forwarding is automatic — **no
1R1W split, no forwarding logic, no hazard scoreboard** beyond the same-line
AMO pacing (§8.4). The tag array stays at S0/S1, so its existing
read-during-write bypasses (`rdw_fill`/`rdw_write`) are unchanged.

### 8.3 The MSHR must NOT be deferred (critical constraint)

[`VX_cache_mshr.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cache/VX_cache_mshr.sv) is strongly coupled
to the bank: its coalescing chain needs `allocate` (S0) and `finalize` (S1)
**exactly one cycle apart**. The tail-find (`prev_idx`) only sees a
predecessor's link once that predecessor finalizes; deferring finalize makes
3+ coalesced same-line misses (e.g. sequential icache fetches to one line)
all link to the same predecessor, orphaning intermediate entries → they never
replay → **bank deadlock** (confirmed empirically — a naive "defer
everything" hung at LATENCY=3 and 4). So the pipeline is **decoupled**:

- **S0/S1 (fixed, 1 cycle apart):** tag compare, replacement victim-select,
  MSHR allocate **and** finalize, replacement update — untouched.
- **stD = S0 + PIPE_EX:** data-array access (pass-through chain off S0).
- **stC = S1 + PIPE_EX:** core response + memory request (off S1), aligned
  with the deferred data output.

`PIPE_EX=0` collapses stD→S0, stC→S1, reproducing the 2-stage bank exactly
(LATENCY=2 gives identical cycle counts).

**Mem-request queue sizing:** the mem-req push now fires `LATENCY` stages
after admission, so the almost-full margin must reserve `LATENCY` slots —
**`MREQ_SIZE > LATENCY`** (else `ALM_FULL ≤ 0` → permanent almost-full →
admission deadlock). The config grows `MREQ_SIZE` by `(LATENCY−2)` to hold
the margin constant.

### 8.4 AMO under elastic latency

The LLC atomic (§5.6) is the most stage-coupled block. Under the elastic pipe
its anchors are re-expressed on the symbolic stage constants rather than
literal `st0`/`st1`: the RMW reads the line word at the data-output stage,
runs the AMO ALU (add/min/max/swap/compare) in the following stage, and
writes back at the commit stage — so deepening *relaxes* the AMO ALU path
(it gets its own stage) rather than complicating it. Same-line AMO chaining
(a chained atomic must observe the previous result) has a commit→visible
round trip of `L−1` cycles, so the `chain_stall`/`commit_busy` pacing scales
with `LATENCY` and **collapses into one depth-sized same-line scoreboard**
(a chained atomic targets a line that scoreboard already marks in-flight).
Non-LLC AMO forward/passthru-replay ordering and LR/SC reservations are
event-ordered (line addresses, not cycles), so they are latency-agnostic
once keyed off the stage constants. At `LATENCY=2` behavior is identical to
today (chain window = 1).

### 8.5 Configuration, cost, and SimX parity

Per-cache knobs in `VX_config.toml` (default 2; raise large LLCs):

```
VX_CFG_L2_LATENCY  = expr: 4 if $VX_CFG_L2_CACHE_SIZE > 65536 else 2
VX_CFG_L3_LATENCY  = expr: 4 if $VX_CFG_L3_CACHE_SIZE > 65536 else 2
VX_CFG_L2_MREQ_SIZE = expr: 4 + ($VX_CFG_L2_LATENCY - 2) + ...   # keep margin
```

The 64 KB threshold: below it the tag/data arrays fit in a few adjacent BRAMs
and the single-cycle path closes; above it (1 MB L2, 2 MB L3) the arrays span
many BRAM columns and the cross-array route cannot meet 3.333 ns.

- **Area** (1 MB L2 bank, depth 2→4): ~+1 % FF (two ~590 b payload stages),
  ~0 BRAM (read/write split is BRAM-native dual-port), a few hundred LUT —
  cheap for a +42 % clock.
- **AMAT:** `Δt_L2 = +2 cyc ⇒ ΔAMAT ≈ m_L1·2 cyc` (~+0.2–0.4 cyc for
  `m_L1≈0.1–0.2`), in the noise against a hundreds-of-cycle `t_mem`. The
  decisive comparison is wall-clock: a single L2 hit is ~3.9 ns slower but
  every cycle everywhere is 42 % faster and the latency is MSHR-hidden.
- **SimX parity:** the SimX bank already models a `latency`-deep pipe
  (`Cache::Config::latency`); the gap is only that L2/L3 use a hardcoded `2`
  ([`cluster.cpp`](../../sim/simx/cluster.cpp),
  [`processor.cpp`](../../sim/simx/processor.cpp)) instead of the macro.
  Sourcing both the RTL bank parameter and the SimX pipe depth from the same
  `VX_CFG_*_LATENCY` keeps them from diverging. The same-line RAW/AMO-chain
  stall must also be modeled in the SimX bank (a marked-line check on
  `pipe_req_` occupancy) so throughput — not just latency — matches.

> Status: `LATENCY=2` is bit-identical to the pre-refactor baseline and
> `LATENCY=3` is functionally validated (rtlsim vecadd/sgemm). `LATENCY=4`
> (with bumped `MREQ_SIZE`), the AMO sweep across depths, SimX parity wiring,
> and the 1 MB-L2 DUT synth confirming WNS ≥ 0 @300 MHz remain to land.
> Depends on the `VX_sp_ram`/`VX_dp_ram` `USE_FAST_BRAM` LUTRAM fix.

---

## 9. Validation

`tests/regression/amo` across all configs, on both SimX and rtlsim:

| config | result |
|---|---|
| 1 core, no L2 | 13/13 |
| 4× L1 → 1× L2 | 12/12 |
| 4× L2 → 1× L3 | 12/12 |

The suite includes `lrsc_counter` (forward-progress repro for §5.1) and
`self_consistency` (per-hart private 64 B line; exercises §5.4/§5.6 and fails
a design lacking the local-invalidate and commit-window serialization).
`atomic_critical` is skipped on multi-core: it relies on plain load/store
inside a critical section, which needs Regime-B coherence (§7).

replacement policy, writeback, clustering, reduced line-size) passes,
confirming the `AMO_ENABLE` plumbing and bank/tag/MSHR changes do not regress

---

## 10. Out of scope / future work

- **Regime-B acquire-invalidate** (§7) — the consumer-side bulk invalidate
  for fence-managed cross-core plain-data visibility.
- **PUSH + directory/snoop-filter** — fence-free cross-core plain-data
  coherence; requires an upstream back-probe channel, per-line sharer
  tracking, an ack/ordering protocol, and recursive re-probing. Not what GPUs
  do; revisit only if a strong cross-core guarantee is ever required.
- **Per-line acquire invalidate** — finer-grained than the whole-cache flash
  invalidate, if profiling shows bulk invalidation hurts hit rate.
- The RTL AMO unit testbench and AMO performance counters
  ([`atomic_memory_operations.md`](atomic_memory_operations.md) §6.3–§6.4).

23	// Per-LLC-bank AMO helper: the RVA RMW kernel + a reservation set.
24	// Reservations are tracked per hart — each hart owns at most one
25	// reservation, which only another hart's committed write to the same
26	// line can break. A hart's reservation is never displaced by another
27	// hart's LR, so a contended LR/SC retry loop always has a winner each
28	// round (forward progress); the prior fixed-size CAM could evict a
29	// hart's reservation between its own LR and SC and livelock when the
30	// number of contending harts exceeded the table size. Owned
31	// synchronously by CacheBank and exercised from processRequests() in
32	// the same cycle as a write-hit.
33	class AmoUnit {
34	public:
35	  // `reservation_size` seeds the table; capacity grows per contending
36	  // hart so forward progress does not depend on the knob.
37	  explicit AmoUnit(uint32_t reservation_size);
38	
39	  // Pure RMW kernel — no reservation touch, no mutation. `unsigned_minmax`
40	  // selects the unsigned variant of MIN/MAX (signed by default).
41	  AmoComputeResult compute(MemOp op, uint8_t width,
42	                           uint64_t old_word, uint64_t rhs,
43	                           bool unsigned_minmax = false) const;
44	
45	  // LR installs a reservation for (hart_id, line_addr). LRU eviction
46	  // when the table is full.
47	  void reserve(uint32_t hart_id, uint64_t line_addr);
48	
49	  // SC's success criterion: an entry exists for (hart_id, line_addr).
50	  bool check(uint32_t hart_id, uint64_t line_addr) const;
51	
52	  // Break reservations on `line_addr` belonging to harts other than
53	  // `except_hart_id`. Triggered on every committed write reaching the
54	  // LLC bank's tag array (writethroughs from above + AMO commits +
55	  // LLC's own write-back write-hit commits).
56	  void invalidate(uint64_t line_addr, uint32_t except_hart_id);
57	
58	  // Drop the reservation matching this entry. Called on a successful
59	  // SC to consume the lock.
60	  void clear(uint32_t hart_id, uint64_t line_addr);
61	
62	  void reset();
63	
64	  // Stats / diagnostics: number of live reservations.
65	  uint32_t capacity() const { return (uint32_t)reservations_.size(); }
66	
67	private:
68	  // hart_id -> reserved line address. One entry per hart at most.
69	  std::unordered_map<uint32_t, uint64_t> reservations_;
70	};

14	`include "VX_cache_define.vh"
15	
16	// Per-LLC-bank AMO helper: the RVA RMW kernel + a small reservation cache.
17	//
18	// Reservations are tracked by a bounded, fixed-size set of stations per bank
19	// (NUM_RS, default load-matched to system concurrency) rather than a slot per
20	// hart. The cache is line-indexed (direct-mapped on the reserved line's low
21	// address bits): the {hart,tag} payload lives in a synchronous block RAM read
22	// one stage ahead (look-ahead address, the VX_cache_tags pattern) so the
23	// registered output lands the same cycle the SC commit decision is made; the
24	// valid bits live in resettable flops (BRAM contents are not reset).
25	//
26	//   LR  : claim the slot for {hart, line}  (overwrites any prior occupant).
27	//   SC  : succeeds iff the slot still holds {hart, line}; the success store
28	//         then clears it through the write path below.
29	//   write: a committed store/RMW to a line clears the slot iff it holds that
30	//          line (tag match) — breaks the reserver, any hart.
31	//
32	// A bounded set with conflict/capacity eviction is RISC-V-legal: SC may fail
33	// spuriously for any reason, and forward progress is a system property (some
34	// hart's SC wins each round). This is how real GPUs/CPUs implement LR/SC, and
35	// it removes the per-hart table's O(NUM_HARTS) storage and CAM.
36	module VX_amo_unit import VX_gpu_pkg::*; #(
37	    parameter NUM_RES_ENTRIES = 4,   // reservation stations per bank (NUM_RS)
38	    parameter LINE_ADDR_BITS  = 32,
39	    parameter DATA_WIDTH      = 64   // ALU operand width (cache word, capped at 64)
40	) (
41	    input  wire                          clk,
42	    input  wire                          reset,
43	    input  wire                          pipe_stall,
44	
45	    // Combinational compute kernel.
46	    input  amo_op_e                      compute_op,
47	    input  wire                          compute_unsigned,
48	    input  wire [1:0]                    compute_width,
49	    input  wire [63:0]                   compute_old,
50	    input  wire [63:0]                   compute_rhs,
51	    output wire [63:0]                   compute_new_word,
52	    output wire [63:0]                   compute_ret_word,
53	
54	    // Reservation activity (single-fire per cycle).
55	    input  wire                          res_reserve,    // LR commit
56	    input  wire                          res_clear,      // SC commit (success or fail)
57	    input  wire                          res_invalidate, // committed write to res_line_addr
58	    input  wire [HART_ID_WIDTH-1:0]      res_hart_id,
59	    input  wire [LINE_ADDR_BITS-1:0]     res_line_addr,   // committed line (stC)
60	    input  wire [LINE_ADDR_BITS-1:0]     res_line_addr_n, // line entering stC next cycle
61	    output wire                          res_check        // SC outcome (1 = match)
62	);
63	
64	    // Pure ALU (no state, no clock).
65	    VX_amo_alu #(
66	        .DATA_WIDTH (DATA_WIDTH)
67	    ) alu (
68	        .op       (compute_op),
69	        .is_unsigned (compute_unsigned),
70	        .width    (compute_width),
71	        .old_word (compute_old),
72	        .rhs      (compute_rhs),
73	        .new_word (compute_new_word),
74	        .ret_word (compute_ret_word)
75	    );
76	
77	    // ============================================================
78	    // Reservation cache: NUM_RS stations, line-indexed.
79	    // ============================================================
80	    // Effective capacity is the next power-of-two >= NUM_RS (>=2), so the line
81	    // index fully covers the storage depth for any requested NUM_RS.
82	    localparam RS_ADDRW    = `UP(`CLOG2(NUM_RES_ENTRIES));
83	    localparam RS_DEPTH    = 1 << RS_ADDRW;
84	    localparam RS_TAG_BITS = LINE_ADDR_BITS - RS_ADDRW;   // {tag,idx} = full line
85	    localparam RS_DATA_W   = HART_ID_WIDTH + RS_TAG_BITS;  // BRAM payload: {hart, tag}
86	
87	    wire en = ~pipe_stall;
88	
89	    // index by the reserved line's low bits; the rest is the stored tag.
90	    // (only the index bits of the look-ahead address are needed)
91	    wire [RS_ADDRW-1:0]    rs_idx   = res_line_addr  [RS_ADDRW-1:0];
92	    wire [RS_ADDRW-1:0]    rs_idx_n = res_line_addr_n[RS_ADDRW-1:0];
93	    wire [RS_TAG_BITS-1:0] rs_tag   = res_line_addr[LINE_ADDR_BITS-1:RS_ADDRW];
94	    `UNUSED_VAR (res_line_addr_n)
95	
96	    // Look-ahead BRAM payload (cache_tags pattern): read at the next index so
97	    // the registered output presents the entry at the commit cycle (stC); the
98	    // LR installs {hart,tag} at the committed index.
99	    wire                 rs_we;
100	    wire [RS_DATA_W-1:0] rs_wdata = {res_hart_id, rs_tag};
101	    wire [RS_DATA_W-1:0] rs_rdata;
102	    VX_dp_ram #(
103	        .DATAW    (RS_DATA_W),
104	        .SIZE     (RS_DEPTH),
105	        .OUT_REG  (1),
106	        .RDW_MODE ("R")
107	    ) rs_store (
108	        .clk   (clk),
109	        .reset (reset),
110	        .read  (en),
111	        .write (rs_we),
112	        .wren  (1'b1),
113	        .waddr (rs_idx),
114	        .raddr (rs_idx_n),
115	        .wdata (rs_wdata),
116	        .rdata (rs_rdata)
117	    );
118	
119	    // Read-during-write forward: an LR installs at the committed index the same
120	    // cycle the next op prefetches it; the registered read would miss it, so
121	    // forward the just-written payload for one cycle.
122	    wire                 rdw_set = rs_we && (rs_idx == rs_idx_n);
123	    reg                  rdw_valid_r;
124	    reg [RS_DATA_W-1:0]  rdw_data_r;
125	    always @(posedge clk) begin
126	        if (reset) begin
127	            rdw_valid_r <= 1'b0;
128	        end else if (en) begin
129	            rdw_valid_r <= rdw_set;
130	            rdw_data_r  <= rs_wdata;
131	        end
132	    end
133	    wire [RS_DATA_W-1:0] rs_data = rdw_valid_r ? rdw_data_r : rs_rdata;
134	
135	    // current entry at the committed line index: valid from flops, payload from BRAM
136	    reg  [RS_DEPTH-1:0]      rs_valid;
137	    wire                     e_valid = rs_valid[rs_idx];
138	    wire [HART_ID_WIDTH-1:0] e_hart  = rs_data[RS_TAG_BITS +: HART_ID_WIDTH];
139	    wire [RS_TAG_BITS-1:0]   e_tag   = rs_data[RS_TAG_BITS-1:0];
140	
141	    wire line_match = e_valid && (e_tag == rs_tag);            // slot holds this line
142	    wire own_match  = line_match && (e_hart == res_hart_id);   // ...reserved by this hart
143	
144	    // SC outcome: this hart's reservation on this line is still live.
145	    assign res_check = own_match;
146	
147	    // LR installs the payload; a matching SC/store clears the valid bit.
148	    assign rs_we = res_reserve && en;
149	    wire   rs_clr = en && ((res_invalidate && line_match)      // any write breaks the reserver
150	                        || (res_clear && own_match));          // SC clears its own
151	
152	    always @(posedge clk) begin
153	        if (reset) begin
154	            rs_valid <= '0;
155	        end else begin
156	            if (rs_we) begin
157	                rs_valid[rs_idx] <= 1'b1;
158	            end else if (rs_clr) begin
159	                rs_valid[rs_idx] <= 1'b0;
160	            end
161	        end
162	    end
163	
164	endmodule

16	// Per-bank AMO engine, instantiated by the bank only when atomics are
17	// enabled. A bank plays exactly one of two roles:
18	//
19	//   IS_LLC=1 (commit): perform the read-modify-write on the line word
20	//     resident at S1, maintain the per-hart reservation table (via
21	//     VX_amo_unit), and inject the result back through the bank pipeline
22	//     as a single-outstanding synthetic writeback.
23	//
24	//   IS_LLC=0 (passthrough): forward the AMO downstream (the LLC does the
25	//     RMW), latch the returned result word, and replay it back to the
26	//     requester. Also enforces same-hart program order at the bank input.
27	//
28	// The two roles are mutually exclusive, so each ties off the other's
29	// outputs and the synthesizer keeps only the selected datapath.
30	module VX_cache_amo import VX_gpu_pkg::*; #(
31	    parameter IS_LLC          = 0,
32	    parameter NUM_RES_ENTRIES = 4,
33	    parameter LINE_ADDR_BITS  = 32,
34	    parameter WORD_WIDTH      = 32,
35	    parameter WORD_SIZE       = 4,
36	    parameter WORD_SEL_WIDTH  = 1,
37	    parameter TAG_WIDTH       = 1,
38	    parameter REQ_SEL_WIDTH   = 1,
39	    parameter ATTR_WIDTH      = 1,
40	    parameter MSHR_SIZE       = 1,
41	    parameter MSHR_ADDR_WIDTH = 1,
42	    parameter WORDS_PER_LINE  = 1,
43	    parameter WORDS_PER_SECTOR = WORDS_PER_LINE, // words per fill/eviction sector (= WORDS_PER_LINE when 1 sector/line)
44	    parameter PIPE_EX         = 0             // deferred-commit depth: _st1 ports lag the S0 lookup by PIPE_EX+1 cycles (0 = classic 2-stage)
45	) (
46	    input  wire                          clk,
47	    input  wire                          reset,
48	    input  wire                          pipe_stall,
49	
50	    // pipeline view
51	    input  amo_req_t                     amo_st0,
52	    input  wire                          valid_st0,
53	    input  wire                          is_creq_st0,
54	    input  wire                          is_hit_st0,
55	    input  wire                          is_replay_st0,
56	    input  amo_req_t                     amo_st1,
57	    input  wire                          valid_st1,
58	    input  wire                          is_creq_st1,
59	    input  wire                          is_hit_st1,
60	    input  wire                          is_replay_st1,
61	    input  wire                          do_write_st1,
62	    input  wire [WORD_WIDTH-1:0]         read_word_st1,
63	    input  wire [WORD_SIZE-1:0]          byteen_st1,
64	    input  wire [WORD_WIDTH-1:0]         write_word_st1,
65	    input  wire [WORD_SEL_WIDTH-1:0]     word_idx_st0,
66	    input  wire [WORD_SEL_WIDTH-1:0]     word_idx_st1,
67	    input  wire [LINE_ADDR_BITS-1:0]     addr_st0,
68	    input  wire [LINE_ADDR_BITS-1:0]     addr_st1,

70	    input  wire [TAG_WIDTH-1:0]          tag_st1,
71	    input  wire [REQ_SEL_WIDTH-1:0]      req_idx_st1,

78	    input  wire                          mshr_allocate_st0,
79	    input  wire [MSHR_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]    mshr_alloc_id_st0,
80	    input  wire [MSHR_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]    mshr_id_st1,
81	    input  wire                          mem_rsp_fire,
82	    input  wire [MSHR_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]    mem_rsp_id,
83	    input  wire [WORDS_PER_SECTOR*WORD_WIDTH-1:0] mem_rsp_data,
84	    input  wire                          is_fill_sel,
85	
86	    // input arbitration (passthrough age-ordering)
87	    input  wire                          core_req_valid,
88	    input  wire                          core_req_is_amo,
89	    input  wire                          core_req_rw,
90	    input  wire [LINE_ADDR_BITS-1:0]     core_req_addr,
91	    input  wire                          rw_st0,
92	    input  wire                          mshr_probe_pending_ld,
93	    input  wire                          mshr_probe_pending_amo,
94	
95	    // commit outputs (tied off when IS_LLC=0)
96	    output wire                          amo_hit_st1,    // AMO commits locally at S1
97	    output wire                          commit_busy,    // commit in flight
98	    output wire                          chain_stall,    // pace same-line chained AMO
99	    output wire                          wb_pending,     // writeback request live
100	    output wire [WORD_WIDTH-1:0]         rsp_data,       // response word on amo_hit_st1
101	    // Read forward: a request reading the AMO'd word while the result is still
102	    // queued/settling must observe those bytes (replays are admitted during
